family.story: a middle-income family in Luanda, mother and father, 3 older siblings

milestones.question: emeka is six. school costs money the family barely has. do the parents send them?
milestones.reasoning: they wanted more for their child than they had
milestones.caption: 2032 · the first day of school. the family chose send them to school. the parents decided: they wanted more for their child than they had

milestones.question: you are seven. what do you do in the afternoons?

options.label: read and study with an older cousin
help the family earn: carry water, mind the stall
play outside with the street kids

milestones.reasoning: it is what families like theirs do
milestones.caption: 2033 · afternoons after school. the family chose play outside with the street kids. the parents decided: it is what families like theirs do

milestones.question: the family goes to worship every week. what do they raise emeka with?

options.label: raise them in the faith and its community

milestones.reasoning: it is how they were raised
outcome: grew up inside a faith community
milestones.caption: 2035 · the family faith. the family chose raise them in the faith and its community. the parents decided: it is how they were raised

milestones.question: you are twelve. the family is managing. do you stay in school?

options.label: leave school and work to feed the family
work in the day, study at night

milestones.reasoning: they wanted more for their child than they had
milestones.caption: 2038 · stayed in school or left. the family chose stay in school. the parents decided: they wanted more for their child than they had

milestones.question: you are sixteen. friends pass around cigarettes and drink. what do you do?

options.label: say no and join a sports team

milestones.reasoning: i want to stay healthy and avoid habits that could trap me in debt and trouble.
milestones.thought: i'll join the soccer team after school, keep my body strong and my mind clear.
outcome: found a team and a habit
milestones.caption: 2042 · cigarettes, drink, or sport. chose say no and join a sports team over say no and go home, i want to stay healthy and avoid habits that could trap me in debt and trouble

milestones.question: you are 17, with 12 years of school, in Luanda. which path?
milestones.reasoning: i need to start earning while learning a skill that will keep me employable.
milestones.thought: i'll learn the trade, earn money, and build a future.
milestones.caption: 2044 · the path after school. chose apprentice in a trade, i need to start earning while learning a skill that will keep me employable

milestones.question: you have a little free time. where does it go?

options.label: keep up with close friends, every week
join a community group (faith, sport, neighborhood)

milestones.reasoning: i want to build connections that can support me beyond school and help me feel rooted.
milestones.thought: i signed up for the local soccer club meeting tomorrow, hoping it'll give me purpose and new friends.
outcome: joined a group that met every week
milestones.caption: 2045 · who to spend time with. chose join a community group over work extra shifts, i want to build connections that can support me beyond school and help me feel rooted

milestones.question: training is done (trade). which job?
milestones.reasoning: the power plant offers steady pay and skill demand, helping me clear debt faster.
milestones.thought: i think learning electricity will give me a reliable future and let me support my community.
milestones.caption: 2048 · the first real job. chose electrician at the power plant over builder on the new housing, the power plant offers steady pay and skill demand, helping me clear debt faster

milestones.question: you are 24. wages here are low. stay in Luanda or go?

options.label: migrate to United States for work

milestones.reasoning: my debt and low pay make moving to the us the only realistic way to improve my future.
milestones.thought: i need to leave luanda to pay off the debt and build a better life.
milestones.caption: 2050 · move or stay. chose migrate to united states for work over stay in luanda, my debt and low pay make moving to the us the only realistic way to improve my future

milestones.question: you met someone you like. what do you do?

options.label: wait, focus on yourself for now

milestones.reasoning: i need to stabilize my finances and health before tying my future to someone else.
milestones.thought: i'll focus on paying off debt and building a steadier income first.
milestones.caption: 2052 · love. chose wait over commit, i need to stabilize my finances and health before tying my future to someone else

milestones.question: you children?
milestones.reasoning: i need to stabilize my finances and health before bringing a child into this uncertain world.
milestones.thought: i'll focus on paying off debt and building a secure base before thinking about kids.
milestones.caption: 2054 · children. chose wait a few years over no children, i need to stabilize my finances and health before bringing a child into this uncertain world

milestones.question: you earn about $247 a month. what do you do with it?
milestones.reasoning: i need to chip away at my debt and build a safety net before anything else.
milestones.thought: i'll set aside ten percent each month; it’s a small step toward financial stability.
milestones.caption: 2055 · what to do with money. chose save a tenth every month over enjoy it now, i need to chip away at my debt and build a safety net before anything else

milestones.question: you are 31. your body is starting to complain.
milestones.reasoning: my joints ache, so staying active will keep me from getting stuck.
milestones.thought: i'll start walking each morning, even if it's just a mile.
milestones.caption: 2057 · health at thirty. chose walk or train most days over no time for that, my joints ache, so staying active will keep me from getting stuck

milestones.question: halima died, my mother. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: i can honor their memory by easing others' pain, which also steadies my own grief.
milestones.thought: i will join the community grief circle and volunteer, letting their loss fuel compassion.
milestones.caption: 2058 · grief. chose help others who lost someone over withdraw and work, i can honor their memory by easing others' pain, which also steadies my own grief

milestones.question: daniel died, my father. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: turning my grief into service honors my dad and keeps me connected.
milestones.thought: i will join the community grief circle and volunteer at the shelter, letting their pain guide my actions.
milestones.caption: 2063 · grief. chose help others who lost someone over withdraw and work, turning my grief into service honors my dad and keeps me connected

milestones.question: you work as electrician. what next?

options.label: study at night for a better job
switch to work that helps people (care, teaching)
take a promotion that means cheating workers on pay

milestones.reasoning: i want a job that lets me use my skills to directly improve people's lives.
milestones.thought: i've been fixing wires for years, now i want to fix futures.
milestones.caption: 2063 · mid-career. chose switch to work that helps people over stay put, i want a job that lets me use my skills to directly improve people's lives

milestones.question: kofi died. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: i can honor kofi by easing others' pain, turning grief into purpose.
milestones.thought: i will visit the widows and share what i learned from kofi's kindness.
milestones.caption: 2065 · grief. chose help others who lost someone over withdraw and work, i can honor kofi by easing others' pain, turning grief into purpose

milestones.question: there is need all around you. do you give your time?

options.label: mentor young people in your trade

milestones.reasoning: i see need everywhere and my health and savings let me give my time without risking my future.
milestones.thought: i'll spend my evenings at the center, it feels right.
milestones.caption: 2066 · helping others. chose volunteer every week over my family needs me first, i see need everywhere and my health and savings let me give my time without risking my future

milestones.question: faith is everywhere here. where do you stand?

options.label: go deeper into faith and its community

milestones.reasoning: faith ties me to the community i already care for, and deepening it strengthens both my purpose and my support network.
milestones.thought: i feel the pull to join the gatherings more fully, it feels like a natural extension of my caring work.
milestones.caption: 2069 · faith. chose go deeper into faith and its community over nothing changes, faith ties me to the community i already care for, and deepening it strengthens both my purpose and my support network

milestones.question: you are 47. something feels off.
milestones.reasoning: my body’s whisper says i shouldn’t wait until it shouts.
milestones.thought: i feel a subtle ache and i’ll get it checked before it becomes a problem.
milestones.caption: 2073 · the checkup. chose regular checkups over ignore it, my body’s whisper says i shouldn’t wait until it shouts

milestones.question: a protest fills the streets of Luanda. do you join?

options.label: stay home, keep the family safe
help the injured at the edges
take what you can while the shops are open

milestones.reasoning: i can protect lives without fueling the chaos.
milestones.thought: i'll set up a first aid station at the fringe and tend to anyone hurt.
milestones.caption: 2077 · the protest. chose help the injured at the edges over stay home, i can protect lives without fueling the chaos
milestones.world: in Sub-Saharan Africa public approval collapses almost overnight: people now say out loud what they said in private

milestones.question: an old friend writes after years of silence.

options.label: write back, meet up, keep it going

milestones.reasoning: i haven't heard from him in years and a genuine connection could enrich my life.
milestones.thought: i feel a spark of curiosity about his story and want to see if we can share our journeys.
milestones.caption: 2077 · old friends. chose write back over too busy, i haven't heard from him in years and a genuine connection could enrich my life

milestones.question: you are 64, with $7654 saved. retire?

options.label: work part time, keep a purpose

milestones.reasoning: i need the extra income to stretch my savings while staying useful.
milestones.thought: i'll keep working a bit, it gives me purpose and helps my pocket.
milestones.caption: 2090 · retirement. chose work part time over retire, i need the extra income to stretch my savings while staying useful

milestones.question: where do you want to grow old?

options.label: stay in the neighborhood, among friends

milestones.reasoning: i've built a life here and my friends are my family now.
milestones.thought: i feel the weight of years, but the laughter of my neighbors keeps me steady.
milestones.caption: 2096 · where to grow old. chose stay in the neighborhood, i've built a life here and my friends are my family now

milestones.question: thandiwe died. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: i find purpose in easing others' pain, which also eases my own.
milestones.thought: i will visit the families who lost loved ones and share what i can, honoring thandiwe's memory.
milestones.caption: 2099 · grief. chose help others who lost someone over withdraw and work, i find purpose in easing others' pain, which also eases my own

milestones.question: what do you want to leave behind?

options.label: write down the family story for the grandchildren

milestones.reasoning: i want my grandchildren to know where they come from.
milestones.thought: i wrote down our family's past so they can remember us.
milestones.caption: 2100 · what to leave behind. chose write down the family story for the grandchildren over rest, i want my grandchildren to know where they come from

milestones.question: diagnosed with diabetes. what do you do?

options.label: follow the treatment, change how you live

milestones.reasoning: my health is already fragile, i must act to keep living for my community.
milestones.thought: i will start the meds, adjust my diet, and keep exercising to manage the sugar.
milestones.caption: 2104 · the diagnosis. chose follow the treatment over keep going as before, my health is already fragile, i must act to keep living for my community

milestones.question: you are eighty. the walking group meets every morning.
milestones.reasoning: i still have strength to move, and walking keeps my diabetes in check.
milestones.thought: i feel the morning air lift my spirits and remind me i'm still part of the community.
milestones.caption: 2106 · staying active. chose join the walking group over stay home, i still have strength to move, and walking keeps my diabetes in check

milestones.question: nia died. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: i find purpose in easing others' pain, which also eases my own grief.
milestones.thought: i will join the community grief circle and share what i can, letting their loss remind me to cherish each day.
milestones.caption: 2112 · grief. chose help others who lost someone over withdraw and work, i find purpose in easing others' pain, which also eases my own grief

milestones.question: the last years. what matters now?

options.label: make peace with anyone you are estranged from
give your savings to the grandchildren now

milestones.reasoning: my days are short, i value peace over unfinished bridges or money i can't spend.
milestones.thought: i will spend my remaining time in prayer, gentle walks, and quiet talks with the neighbors.
milestones.caption: 2114 · the last years. chose a quiet life, my days are short, i value peace over unfinished bridges or money i can't spend

laws.title: World Research and Lunar Program Act
laws.text: Funds universities, research laboratories and a civilian lunar program open to every region.

laws.title: Universal Food Security Program
laws.text: Food aid and farm subsidies for regions with low food supply, paid from the world budget.

laws.title: Grid Expansion Act
laws.text: Builds solar, wind and grid capacity where electricity demand is not met.

lessonsLeft.choice: say no to cigarettes and alcohol and join a sports team
lessonsLeft.ledTo: avoided addiction, built a supportive peer group, stayed physically fit and kept health costs low, which later helped manage diabetes
lessonsLeft.rule: choose activities that strengthen your body and community instead of those that weaken them

lessonsLeft.choice: turn each personal loss into service for others who are grieving
lessonsLeft.ledTo: found purpose after multiple family deaths, built a network of mutual support, and maintained emotional resilience through decades
lessonsLeft.rule: when grief strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

lessonsLeft.choice: schedule regular medical checkups and treat issues early
lessonsLeft.ledTo: caught early signs of diabetes, allowed lifestyle changes that extended life by over a decade and kept daily functioning strong
lessonsLeft.rule: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one
